theme: Abijah, Asa, Chronicles’ portrait of reform
readingInstruction: Read 2 Chronicles 13:1-16:14. Abijah speaks to Jeroboam, Asa seeks the LORD and has peace, and then Asa relies on Syria and on physicians and not the LORD. Watch how his story changes.
settingTheScene: Abijah, king of Judah, faces Jeroboam’s much larger army. Then his son Asa begins a long reign with a great reform and thirty-five years of peace. But in his later years, he trusts in a human alliance instead of God, rejects the prophet, and dies after seeking help from physicians only. The Chronicler makes him an example of a good start and a poor finish.
observation: “God is with us at our head, and his priests with their battle trumpets to sound the call to battle against you” (13:12).
“And the men of Judah cried out. And when the men of Judah shouted, God defeated Jeroboam” (13:15).
“Thus the men of Israel were subdued at that time, and the men of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD” (13:18).
“And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God” (14:2).
“LORD, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you” (14:11).
“The LORD is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you” (15:2).
“For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless toward him” (16:9).
“Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but sought help from the physicians” (16:12).
interpretation:
The Chronicler tells the stories as case studies in dependence. Abijah is outnumbered two to one and ambushed. But he stands on a hill and speaks to Jeroboam, reminding him of God’s covenant with David and of Jeroboam’s golden calves. When the battle is joined, Judah cries out to the LORD, the priests blow trumpets, and God routs the enemy. “They relied on the LORD.” The word means to lean.

Asa’s first years are the model. He removes the foreign altars and high places, commands Judah to seek the LORD, and gets peace. When a million Ethiopians come against him, he prays one of the best prayers of the Bible: “LORD, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak.” God gives victory.

The prophet Azariah then gives the principle that summarizes the Chronicler’s theology: “The LORD is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.” Asa and the people enter a covenant to seek the LORD with all their heart and soul, and “he was found by them.” He even deposes his own grandmother for idolatry.

But in the thirty-sixth year, Baasha of Israel comes against him, and Asa takes the temple’s silver and gold to hire the king of Syria. It works, politically. Then the seer Hanani rebukes him: “Because you relied on the king of Syria, and did not rely on the LORD your God… the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless.” Asa’s response is to throw the prophet into prison and oppress some of the people.

The saddest note: when he is diseased in his feet, he “did not seek the LORD, but sought help from the physicians.” The point is not that doctors are wrong, but that he sought only them. He had lost the habit of dependence.
connection: Proverbs 3:5-6: “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.” Jeremiah 17:5-8 contrasts those who trust in man with those who trust in the LORD. 2 Corinthians 12:9: “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Philippians 3:13-14 speaks of pressing on. Hebrews 3:14 warns that we share in Christ if we hold our original confidence firm to the end. John 15:5: “Apart from me you can do nothing.”
application:
Pray Asa’s prayer: “There is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak.”

Think about a place in your life where you rely on human solutions only. Bring God into it.

Pray for finishing well. Ask God to keep you dependent on him in the later seasons of life.
prayerPrompts: Tell God that you rely on him, not on your own strength.
Thank him that there is none like him to help the weak.
Ask him to keep you from turning to others first.
